The multiplayer smoke test is now passing on the new port 4747, which means the core server logic and client connections are stable. The next logical step is to verify that the front‑end assets are being built correctly and that the UI renders as expected in a browser. The repository includes a Vite (or similar) build script invoked via `npm run build`, which compiles the client-side code into static files served by the Node server. 

I should run the build command to ensure there are no compilation errors. Since the previous steps already restarted the server on port 4747, the built files will be served at `http://localhost:4747`. To quickly confirm the visual output without manual interaction, I can use Chrome in headless mode to capture screenshots of the main menu page and the in‑game view (the latter is accessed via the `#screenshot` hash route). 

The screenshots will be saved to the temporary directory (`$env:TEMP`) with distinct filenames (`fps_menu.png` and `fps_game.png`). After taking them, I need to verify that both files exist, which will serve as a simple check that the headless browser was able to load the pages and that the build succeeded.

Because the build might take a little time, I’ll give the whole operation a generous timeout of two minutes. I’ll also pipe the output of `npm run build` to capture only the last three lines – this should surface any errors if they occur, while keeping the output concise.

Putting this together, the appropriate PowerShell command is:

- Run `npm run build` and capture the tail of its output.
- Launch Chrome headless to screenshot the menu page.
- Launch Chrome headless again to screenshot the game page (`#screenshot`).
- Finally, test that both screenshot files exist.

All of these steps can be combined into a single PowerShell `input` for the tool, with a description that reflects the purpose (“Rebuild and screenshot menu and game views”) and a timeout of 120 000 ms.

Thus, the next tool call should be exactly:

```json
{
  "command": "npm run build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 3; & \"C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe\" --headless=new --window-size=1280,720 --screenshot=\"$env:TEMP\\fps_menu.png\" --virtual-time-budget=5000 --no-first-run \"http://localhost:4747\" 2>&1 | Out-Null; & \"C:\\Program Files\\Google\\Chrome\\Application\\chrome.exe\" --headless=new --window-size=1280,720 --screenshot=\"$env:TEMP\\fps_game.png\" --virtual-time-budget=5000 --no-first-run \"http://localhost:4747/#screenshot\" 2>&1 | Out-Null; (Test-Path \"$env:TEMP\\fps_menu.png\") -and (Test-Path \"$env:TEMP\\fps_game.png\")",
  "description": "Rebuild and screenshot menu and game views",
  "timeout": 120000
}
```

This will both validate the build and give me visual confirmation that the UI loads correctly on the new port.
